title: GI Bill® for Welding School: How To Check Approval and UTI Campus Availability
summary: Wondering whether VA education benefits apply to welding school? See how to check approval, what VA may pay for and how UTI welding campuses compare.
body_markdown:
Veterans may be able to use the GI Bill for welding school, as long as the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has approved the specific welding program at that school location.21


The VA makes the final call on your eligibility and your benefit amounts.


Before using the[GI Bill for trade school](https://www.uti.edu/blog/tips/gi-bill-for-trade-school) , confirm that your chosen program is approved at the campus you plan to attend, because approval can vary by program and location.


That's why this page shows you how to check instead of handing you a blanket yes.


Universal Technical Institute (UTI) offers the[Welding Technology program, a](https://www.uti.edu/programs/welding) nd VA benefits can be used for this program at most campuses 1 The table below shows the VA benefits status for each UTI welding campus.


This page is for veterans, service members and family members weighing different welding schools. It covers how to tell if a program has VA approval, the VA benefits that can apply, what the Post-9/11 GI Bill may pay for and the status of each UTI campus.


## Does the GI Bill Cover Welding School?


The GI Bill can be used for welding school when the VA has approved the specific welding program at the specific school location. Ultimately the VA makes the final decision on eligibility and benefit amounts.


For welding programs that award a certificate or diploma instead of a college degree, VA’s[non-college degree programs](https://www.va.gov/education/about-gi-bill-benefits/how-to-use-benefits/non-college-degree-programs/) page explains how benefits are calculated based on the benefit you use and your enrollment.


### Key Takeaways


- Using the GI Bill for welding school comes down to four things: program approval, where to check it, what the VA pays and how campuses differ.
- Approval is tied to the specific welding program and the specific location where you want to train, so check both before you count on VA benefits.
- The VA's[GI Bill Comparison Tool](https://www.va.gov/education/gi-bill-comparison-tool/) is where you can check to see if the program you’re interested in is approved, and the School Certifying Official, the school staff member who handles VA paperwork, confirms it.
- Under the Post-9/11 GI Bill, the VA can pay for tuition and fees, a monthly housing allowance, and books and supplies, but exact amounts will depend on your eligibility.


## How To Check Whether a Welding Program Is GI Bill-Approved


To check whether a welding program is GI Bill approved, look up the exact school location and program in the VA's GI Bill Comparison Tool, then confirm what you find with the school. The check takes five steps:


1. Confirm your eligibility and get your Certificate of Eligibility from the VA. This VA document shows which benefit you have and how much entitlement you have left.


2. Open the[GI Bill Comparison Tool](https://www.va.gov/education/gi-bill-comparison-tool/) . It's how you search for schools and employers with programs approved for veterans' benefits.


3. Search for the school and open the profile for the location you'd attend.


4. Review the programs listed for that location and any caution flags VA displays. A caution flag means the VA or another federal agency has looked at a school or program more closely.


5. Contact the School Certifying Official at the school to confirm what you found.


## VA Education Benefits That Can Apply to Welding Training


Four types of VA benefits can apply to welding training, and which one you qualify for will depend on your service history or your relationship to a veteran.


- **Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33)** may apply if you served on active duty after Sept. 10, 2001, and eligible service members can transfer unused benefits to a spouse or dependent child.
- **Chapters 30 and 1606** , the Montgomery GI Bill Active Duty and Selected Reserve programs, may cover non-college degree programs.
- **Chapter 35, Survivors' and Dependents' Educational Assistance (DEA),** may apply to dependents and surviving spouses of veterans or service members.
- **Chapter 31, Veteran Readiness and Employment,** is a separate benefit for veterans with a service-connected disability.


The VA decides who qualifies for each benefit. Through[UTI military and veteran services](https://www.uti.edu/support-services/military-veteran-services) , UTI's Military Admissions team can help with eligibility requirements and paperwork.


For the military side of welding, including support welder roles, see[welding careers in the military](https://www.uti.edu/blog/welding/military-support-welder) .


## What the GI Bill May Pay for in Welding School


For eligible students enrolled in an approved welding program, the Post-9/11 GI Bill (Chapter 33) may help cover:


- **Tuition and required fees:** Payments toward approved training costs, sent directly to the school.
- **Housing:** A monthly allowance for students who meet the applicable eligibility and enrollment requirements.
- **Books and supplies:** A separate payment to help with these expenses.


Award amounts depend on your eligibility, enrollment details, training location and other factors, with different rules applying to tuition, housing and books and supplies payments. Rates and payment limits can change, so review the VA’s current[Post-9/11 GI Bill rates](https://www.va.gov/education/benefit-rates/post-9-11-gi-bill-rates/) and confirm your benefits with VA as you plan for school costs. UTI Welding Campuses and VA Benefit Availability


UTI offers welding training at multiple campuses, but VA education benefits may not be available at every location.²⁰ Visit the[Welding Technology program](https://www.uti.edu/programs/welding) page to explore current campus options.


Before enrolling, contact UTI’s Military Admissions team to confirm benefit availability at the campus you’re considering and ask what paperwork you’ll need. You can connect with the team through[UTI military and veteran services](https://www.uti.edu/support-services/military-veteran-services) .How VA Benefits Work With Other Financial Aid Options


VA benefits are one potential funding source for welding school, and students can look at other sources too. The Free Application for Federal Student Aid (FAFSA) is the federal aid application, and[UTI's Financial Aid team](https://www.uti.edu/financial-aid) can help with the application process.10 Each source has its own eligibility rules, so read the details for the ones you're considering.


Award amounts for UTI's[scholarships and grants](https://www.uti.edu/financial-aid/scholarships-grants) vary from student to student. For a wider look at paying for welding school, see how[financing welding trade school](https://www.uti.edu/blog/welding/financing-welding-trade-school-options) works.


## FAQs About Using the GI Bill for Welding School


### What happens if the welding program I want is not GI Bill approved?


If a welding program isn't GI Bill approved, VA education benefits won't apply to it, so the next step is to look for an approved alternative. Search other locations or programs in the GI Bill Comparison Tool and ask the School Certifying Official at the school about the program's approval status. VA decides eligibility.


### Does the GI Bill pay a housing allowance if I attend welding school less than full time?


The Post-9/11 GI Bill pays a prorated monthly housing allowance when your rate of pursuit is more than 50% and it pays none at half time or less. Rate of pursuit is how much school you attend, which VA measures in credits or, for clock-hour programs, in clock hours you're scheduled to attend each week. Your eligibility percentage and class location also change the amount, so check the VA's rates page for your situation.


### Does the GI Bill cover welding certification tests?


The GI Bill may cover costs for approved licensing or certification tests, so a welding certification test is covered only if VA has approved it. You must already be covered by a VA education benefit such as the Post-9/11 GI Bill, and the GI Bill Comparison Tool's licenses, certifications and prep courses search shows whether a test is approved. The VA's page on licensing and certification tests lists the reimbursement rules. For the common welding credentials, see welding certifications.


### Can the GI Bill be used for a welding apprenticeship?


A welding apprenticeship qualifies for the GI Bill only when the VA has approved the employer's training program, and the GI Bill Comparison Tool shows which programs are approved. Payment works differently than attending a trade school: you get a monthly payment for living expenses, plus a books and supplies amount under the Post-9/11 GI Bill. Active-duty service members can't use on-the-job training. See the VA's[on-the-job training and apprenticeships](https://www.va.gov/education/about-gi-bill-benefits/how-to-use-benefits/on-the-job-training-apprenticeships/) page for the current rules.


### Can the GI Bill be used for more than one training program?


[The GI Bill can pay for more than one training program](https://www.va.gov/education/about-gi-bill-benefits/how-to-use-benefits/non-college-degree-programs/) . After you finish a first program, you can use any benefits you have left for courses in another program. Your Certificate of Eligibility shows how much entitlement remains.


## Next Steps for Welding Training With VA Benefits


Using the GI Bill for welding school starts by checking whether the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs (VA) has approved the program at the location you'd attend. The VA's GI Bill Comparison Tool is where you confirm that approval, and the school can confirm it too. From there, your eligibility percentage determines the exact benefits available to you.


Universal Technical Institute (UTI) offers the[Welding Technology](https://www.uti.edu/programs/welding) program, which includes hands-on training in metal inert gas (MIG), tungsten inert gas (TIG), stick and flux-cored welding processes. VA approval varies by campus.


To ask about VA education benefits and campus availability for welding training,[request information online](https://www.uti.edu/request-info) or call 1-(800) 834-7308. If you’re ready to get started,[apply now](https://www.uti.edu/forms/enroll-now) .
